output.summary: Observation: A deployment occurred, after which error rates increased. No rollback has been attempted. Unknown: which service(s) deployed, what change was made, what the baseline error rate was, what the current error rate is, whether errors are user-facing or internal, and whether the increase is correlated or coincidental with the deployment.
blockers: No rollback has been initiated despite elevated error rates, suggesting either no alerting/policy is in place or the team is unaware of the severity
Unknown whether the deployment is to a single service or multiple services, making isolation difficult
No information on whether errors are deterministic (e.g., crash, 500) or intermittent (e.g., timeouts, degraded latency)
No known baseline or threshold for acceptable error rate, so severity is undetermined
No visibility into whether downstream dependencies were also changed or affected
nextActions: Check deployment logs and release notes to identify exactly what changed (files, configs, dependencies, feature flags)
Compare current error rate against the pre-deployment baseline using monitoring dashboards (e.g., Grafana, Datadog) over the same time window
Filter error logs by time range post-deployment to identify error patterns, stack traces, or specific endpoints affected
Check whether the error increase is isolated to the deployed service or propagates to dependent services
Review recent config or environment variable changes that may accompany the deployment
If errors are deterministic and tied to the deployed version, prepare and evaluate a rollback plan (read-only: verify previous artifact is available, check rollback procedure docs)
Verify whether health checks or canary analysis tools were configured and whether they triggered alerts
Document findings before any write action is taken, noting what is confirmed vs. inferred

output.summary: User reports being unable to sign in due to an expired session error.
missingInformation: Whether the issue is consistent or intermittent
Whether clearing cookies and cache resolves the issue
Whether the issue occurs for other users or only this account
Any recent changes to account, permissions, or environment
Error code or screenshot of the error
How long sessions typically last before expiring
output.proposedReply:
Hi there, thanks for reaching out. I'm sorry you're seeing an expired session error when trying to sign in. To help us investigate and get you back in quickly, could you please share the following details?

1. Which browser and version are you using?
2. What device and operating system are you on?
3. Does the error happen consistently, or does it come and go?
4. Have you tried clearing your browser cookies and cache, or signing in from a private/incognito window?
5. Are other users on your team experiencing the same issue, or is it isolated to your account?
6. Are you connected via a VPN, corporate proxy, or restrictive network?
7. If you have a screenshot of the error or an error code, that would be very helpful.
8. How long after logging in does the session typically expire?

Once we have this information we can narrow down the cause and suggest the right fix. Thanks!
